p: Seasonal demand is a recurring and reasonably predictable change in the number of customers, orders or sales a business receives during particular periods.
Seasonal demand patterns may repeat daily, weekly, monthly or annually.
In the Midwest, seasonal demand can affect customer activity, staffing, supply chains, inventory and operating costs, depending on the business and location.
Winter conditions can affect travel, deliveries, construction and foot traffic while increasing heating and maintenance costs.
Spring and summer can bring increased activity in construction, agriculture, tourism, outdoor recreation and seasonal events.
Severe storms, flooding, heatwaves or other weather conditions can disrupt business operations.
In autumn, businesses may experience changes in consumer spending, school-related activity, harvest cycles and preparation for the holiday season.
Holidays, school calendars, tourism, agricultural cycles, local events and changes in customer buying habits can influence seasonal demand.
Understanding seasonal patterns can help businesses plan ahead, make the most of busy periods and prepare for quieter ones.

d49aed6f4bac0692faa82278af650419be4efd05.c: This Dupaco business resource page explains who qualifies as a beneficial owner for reporting to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).
p: A beneficial owner is a person who directly or indirectly exercises substantial control over a reporting company or owns or controls at least 25% of its ownership interests.
A person may qualify as a beneficial owner through both substantial control and ownership interests.
A company must report everyone considered a beneficial owner, regardless of how many people qualify, according to FinCEN.

Exceptions to the beneficial ownership definition include minor children, individuals acting on behalf of an actual beneficiary, employees, inheritors with only a future interest through inheritance, and company creditors.
Most U.S. companies will need to report who owns and/or runs the company.
